panels.title: GPU Utilization
panels.description: Percent of time the GPU was actively processing.

panels.title: GPU Utilization per Pod
panels.description: GPU utilization per process, summed per pod.

panels.title: SM Activity
panels.description: Percent of cycles where an SM had at least one warp resident.

panels.title: SM Occupancy
panels.description: Percent of number of warps resident on an SM.

panels.title: Tensor Core Utilization
panels.description: Percent of cycles when any tensor pipe was active, and per pipe: HMMA, IMMA, DFMA.

panels.title: FP & Integer Utilization
panels.description: Percent of cycles when the FP64, FP32, FP16 and integer pipes were active.

panels.title: Cache Hit Rates
panels.description: Percent of requests to host memory and to peer memory that were cache hits. Host-memory hits require a Grace-coupled platform; peer-memory hits require NVLink-equipped GPUs.

panels.title: Cache Miss Rates
panels.description: Percent of requests to host memory and to peer memory that were cache misses. Host-memory misses require a Grace-coupled platform; peer-memory misses require NVLink-equipped GPUs.

panels.title: Memory Used vs Total
panels.description: Memory in use, against the memory installed on the card.

panels.title: Memory Used Over Time
panels.description: Memory in use.

panels.title: Memory Held by Each Pod
panels.description: Memory in use per process, summed per pod.

panels.title: Memory Bandwidth Utilization
panels.description: Percent of cycles the device memory interface is active.

panels.title: PCIe Transmission Throughput
panels.description: Rate of data received by, and transmitted from, the GPU over PCIe.

panels.title: NVLink Transmission Throughput
panels.description: Rate of data received by, and transmitted from, the GPU over NVLink. Requires NVLink-equipped GPUs.

panels.title: Chip to Chip Bandwidth
panels.description: Total bytes received over, and transmitted over, the chip-to-chip link. Requires a Grace-coupled platform.

panels.title: GPU Power Usage
panels.description: Power usage of the device in watts.

panels.title: GPU Temperature
panels.description: Current GPU device temperature in Celsius.

panels.title: Clock Frequencies
panels.description: Current SM and memory clock frequency in MHz.

panels.title: Clocks Throttle Reasons
panels.description: Fraction of the interval each throttle reason was active.

panels.title: Entitlement
panels.description: The pod granted this device. Constant 1; the identity is in the labels.

panels.title: Metric Support Matrix
panels.description: Whether an entity can produce a metric: 1 supported, 0 not supported, absent when unknown.

panels.title: Memory Bandwidth Utilization
panels.description: Percent of cycles the device memory interface is active.

panels.title: Metric Support Matrix
panels.description: Whether an entity can produce a metric: 1 supported, 0 not supported, absent when unknown.

panels.title: Total CUDA Kernel Launches
panels.description: Total kernels launched by the selected pods and GPUs across the current time window. The single clearest liveness signal this dashboard has — zero while a pod is Running means nothing reached the GPU during the window; check Compute Activity for a per-pod breakdown.

panels.title: Total CUDA Errors
panels.description: Total failed CUDA driver calls (non-zero return code) in the window, across every probed function. Not yet observed on this cluster — every traced call has returned success so far, which is a healthy result, not a gap. Drill into the Errors row for which function and code the moment this goes non-zero.

panels.title: Total HAMi OOM Events
panels.description: Total allocations HAMi's interception library refused because a pod exceeded its memory quota. Not yet observed on this cluster: no traced workload has hit a HAMi memory limit, consistent with the compute-throttle signal (Errors row) also never firing here. A strong signal to raise the memory quota the moment it appears.

panels.title: CUDA Kernel Launch Rate
panels.description: Kernels submitted to the GPU per second, per pod — the clearest liveness signal for a GPU workload. A sudden drop while the pod is still Running usually means a stall; check the Errors row or GPU memory (GPU Hardware dashboard) next.

panels.title: CUDA Graph Launch Rate
panels.description: How often the workload replays a captured CUDA Graph (cuGraphLaunch) — one call submits a whole batched sequence of kernels, so it never shows up in the per-kernel counter to the left. Not yet observed on this cluster: neither gpu-burn nor the resnet50/shufflenet_v2 validation run uses graph-mode execution (torch.cuda.graphs, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM). Non-zero once populated means the framework is using graph optimisation.

panels.title: Host-Side CUDA Kernel Launch Latency Distribution
panels.description: Full distribution of how long the HOST waited inside the launch call, across the selected pods. A P95/P99 line (right) can hide a bimodal stall — most launches fast, a distinct second cluster slow — where this heatmap shows two separate bands instead of one blurred average. Look for a second warm band appearing above the main one before trusting a P95 line alone.

panels.title: Host-Side CUDA Kernel Launch Latency P95/P99
panels.description: How long the HOST waited to submit work, not GPU runtime — launches are asynchronous. Rising here while the Kernel Launch Rate stays flat means the bottleneck is the CPU or the input pipeline, not the GPU. See the heatmap to the left for the full distribution; a P95 line can under-report a bimodal stall.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_kernel_launch_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_kernel_launch_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Pods Ranked by CUDA Activity
panels.description: Every pod that launched at least one CUDA kernel in the selected window, ranked by launch count — the fastest way to see which workloads are actually doing CUDA work right now versus merely holding a GPU allocation. Cross-check against GPU Hardware's entitlement table to see who holds a GPU without using it.

panels.title: GPU Memory Allocation Rate
panels.description: Bytes/second successfully allocated on the GPU (device, managed, pinned-host and stream-ordered allocators). Not yet observed on this cluster. PyTorch's caching allocator takes a few large allocations at warm-up and then reuses that arena, so steady-state training produces almost no cudaMalloc calls. Once populated, steady growth without matching frees (right) indicates a memory leak.

panels.title: GPU Memory Allocation Call Rate
panels.description: Allocation calls per second, independent of size. Not yet observed on this cluster, for the same caching-allocator reason as the byte rate to the left. Once populated, many small calls in a row (high call rate, low average size) indicates fragmentation risk rather than a caching allocator reusing its pool.

panels.title: Average Memory Allocation Size
panels.description: Bytes per allocation call, averaged over the rate window. Not yet observed on this cluster — it depends on the same allocation-call family above, which PyTorch's caching allocator makes nearly silent after warm-up. A very small average, once populated, suggests the workload isn't using a caching allocator at all.

targets.expr: sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid) (rate(ebpf_cuda_memory_allocations_bytes_total{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid) (rate(ebpf_cuda_memory_allocations_calls_total{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])), 1)

panels.title: GPU Memory Free Rate
panels.description: Bytes/second of GPU memory freed, including host-pinned unregister. Not yet observed on this cluster — PyTorch's caching allocator holds onto its arena instead of freeing back to the driver during steady-state training, the same reason the allocation family is silent. Once populated, pair with Allocation Rate: allocations persistently exceeding frees is the leak signature.

panels.title: GPU Memory Free Call Rate
panels.description: Free calls per second. Not yet observed on this cluster, same reason as Free Rate above. Once populated, pair with Allocation Call Rate: a large persistent imbalance indicates a leak or over-eager release.

panels.title: Memory Copy Traffic by Direction
panels.description: Data movement per second, split by direction (cuda_memcpy_kind). Host-to-device bytes are usually the input pipeline; sustained high copy with low kernel activity in Compute Activity means the GPU is being starved. Device-to-device dominates during NCCL all-reduce in multi-GPU training.

panels.title: Memset Traffic — Sync vs Async
panels.description: Bytes/second cleared on the device (cudaMemset / cudaMemsetAsync), split by whether the call blocks the host. High sync-memset rates are often wasteful buffer re-initialisation that could be replaced with the async form or with reuse.

panels.title: P2P Peer Copy Traffic
panels.description: Direct GPU-to-GPU transfer bytes/second over NVLink/PCIe, bypassing the host. Not yet observed on this cluster: every validated workload (gpu-burn, resnet50/shufflenet_v2) ran on a single shared card, so there was no peer traffic to trace. Non-zero once populated only for workloads that copy directly between devices — normal for multi-GPU training, otherwise worth investigating.

panels.title: CUDA Errors per Interval
panels.description: New CUDA errors per interval, broken down by which function failed and its return code (e.g. 2 = out of memory, 1 = invalid argument, 400 = invalid handle). Not yet observed on this cluster — catches failures a workload swallows without logging, the moment any traced call starts returning non-zero.

targets.expr: sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, cuda_function, cuda_error_code) (increase(ebpf_cuda_errors_total{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: HAMi OOM Events per Interval
panels.description: New HAMi quota-denied allocations per interval, by function and memory kind. Not yet observed on this cluster — no traced pod has hit a HAMi memory quota. Non-zero once populated means increase the ResourceClaim memory limit for that pod.

targets.expr: sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, cuda_function, hami_oom_mem_kind, hami_oom_error_code) (increase(ebpf_hami_oom_events_total{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: HAMi Compute Throttle Latency P95/P99
panels.description: How long HAMi's rate limiter delayed each kernel launch before passing it to the driver — the compute quota being enforced, measured directly. Not yet observed on this cluster: HAMi's interception library is injected into the gpu-burn pods, but this metric staying empty is the second independent signal (alongside near-50/50 SM utilization against a 3:1 grant — see the NVML exporter notes) that HAMi is not actually enforcing its compute-core grant here. Persistently high values, once populated, mean the SM quota is too tight.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_hami_compute_throttle_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_hami_compute_throttle_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: HAMi OOM Events — Detail Table
panels.description: All HAMi OOM tuples in the selected time range, even for pods that have already exited — useful after the fact since kernel-level metrics disappear once a pod is gone. Not yet observed on this cluster; will populate at the same moment as the two panels above.

targets.expr: max_over_time(sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, cuda_function, hami_oom_mem_kind, hami_oom_error_code) (ebpf_hami_oom_events_total{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"})[$__range:])

panels.title: CUDA Stream Sync Latency P95/P99
panels.description: Host-thread wait time in cuStreamSynchronize — how long the CPU blocked for one specific stream to drain. High values indicate GPU backpressure on that stream: the host has more work queued than the GPU can drain.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_stream_sync_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_stream_sync_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: CUDA Device Sync Latency P95/P99
panels.description: Host-thread wait time in cuCtxSynchronize / cuDeviceSynchronize — a full-device barrier, stricter than a stream sync. Not yet observed on this cluster: gpu-burn loops kernels without a device-wide barrier, and the training benchmark synchronizes at the stream level instead. Sustained high P99, once populated, is a strong backpressure signal and serializes the whole pipeline, not just one stream.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_device_sync_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_device_sync_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: CUDA Event Sync Latency P95/P99
panels.description: Host-thread wait time in cuEventSynchronize — how long the CPU blocked waiting on one specific recorded CUDA event, finer-grained than a stream or device sync. Not yet observed on this cluster: neither validation workload uses event-based wait/dependency tracking.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_event_sync_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_event_sync_duration_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: CUDA Event Elapsed Time P95/P99
panels.description: Real on-device execution time between two CUDA events (cudaEventElapsedTime) — the one genuine hardware timing this exporter can report; every other duration on this dashboard is host-side wait. Not yet observed on this cluster: it only appears for a workload that explicitly times itself with paired CUDA events, which neither gpu-burn nor the training benchmark does. A bonus signal when present, never a dependency — its absence does not mean the GPU is idle.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_event_elapsed_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_event_elapsed_seconds_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Kernel Grid Size P95/P99
panels.description: Distribution of grid size (gridX × gridY × gridZ = total thread blocks) requested per kernel launch. P95/P99 reveal the largest kernels being scheduled — pair with Block Size to see how much parallelism the workload is asking for per launch.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_kernel_grid_size_total_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_kernel_grid_size_total_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Kernel Block Size P95/P99
panels.description: Distribution of block size (blockX × blockY × blockZ = threads per block) requested per kernel launch. With Grid Size, this explains an SM occupancy figure on the GPU Hardware dashboard — small blocks with low occupancy there usually means the launch configuration itself is limiting parallelism, not GPU capacity.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_kernel_block_size_total_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_kernel_block_size_total_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Kernel Shared Memory Request Size P95/P99
panels.description: Distribution of shared memory requested per kernel launch. High requests limit how many blocks can be resident on one SM at once, capping occupancy even when the grid asks for plenty of parallelism — a kernel that looks under-occupied on GPU Hardware may simply be requesting too much shared memory per block.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_kernel_shared_memory_bytes_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (k8s_namespace_name, k8s_pod_name, k8s_pod_uid, gpu_uuid, le) (rate(ebpf_cuda_kernel_shared_memory_bytes_bucket{k8s_pod_name=~"$pod",gpu_uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__rate_interval])))
